page: OVHcloud c2-120 is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel processor running at 3.0 GHz. The hardware configuration provides 32 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, meaning hyperthreading is disabled. It is equipped with 120.0 GB of RAM, equating to 3.75 GB of memory per core. Local storage consists of a 400 GB SSD, and the instance includes a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results place the c2-120 in the average performance tier for most workloads, with a notable exception in multi-threaded decompression. The instance achieved a strong score of 253.18 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, placing it in the top 25% of tested systems. Other CPU metrics, such as the stress-ng multi-core score of 49032.04 and the PassMark CPU score of 40620.12, fall within the middle 50% range. Memory bandwidth is measured at 113.21 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 38.36 GB/sec for large-block write operations.

While the server demonstrates stable average performance across standard tasks like static web serving at 21.65 GB/sec and database operations, it exhibits limitations in text generation for large language models. LLM text generation speeds are poor, yielding 37.21 tokens/sec for a small 135M model and 6.29 tokens/sec for a medium 7B model. This indicates a tradeoff where the server is highly capable for parallel CPU-bound tasks like software compilation and decompression, but less suited for real-time generative AI workloads. It is best utilized for compute-heavy batch processing, web serving, and software development pipelines.
description: The OVHcloud c2-120 is a compute-optimized server instance built on the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. It features a dedicated Intel processor with 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 3.0 GHz, offering a single thread per core. The system is equipped with 120.0 GB of RAM, a local 400 GB SSD, and 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Performance benchmarks show average results across most metrics, including a PassMark CPU score of 40620.12 and a static web serving throughput of 21.65 GB/sec. However, it excels in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, reaching 253.18 GB/sec. Conversely, text generation for LLMs is a notable bottleneck, with poor token-per-second rates. This instance is highly suited for dedicated compute workloads, software compilation, and parallel batch processing, but less optimal for generative AI inference.
